chunks: Muhammad ibn al-Hasan ibn Ahmad ibn al-Walid narrated to me from Muhammad ibn al-Hasan al-Saffar, from Muhammad ibn Abd al-Jabbar, from Abd al-Rahman ibn Abi Najran, from Amir ibn Jud'ah, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:

When you visit al-Husayn (peace be upon him), say: All praise is to Allah, and may Allah bless Muhammad the Prophet and his family, and peace be upon him and them, and the mercy of Allah and His blessings. May Allah bless you, O Abu Abdillah. May Allah curse the one who killed you, and the one who shared in your blood, and the one to whom this was conveyed and was pleased with it. We are free from them before Allah, three times.

My father (may Allah have mercy on him) narrated to me from Sa'd ibn Abdillah, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Abd al-Rahman ibn Abi Najran, from Muhammad ibn Abi Umayr, from Amir ibn Jud'ah, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:

When you visit al-Ha'ir, say: All praise is to Allah, and may Allah bless Muhammad and the people of his house, and peace be upon him and them, peace, and the mercy of Allah and His blessings. Peace be upon you, O Abu Abdillah. May Allah curse the one who killed you, and the one who shared in your blood, and the one to whom this was conveyed and was pleased with it. We are free from them before Allah.

key_terms.أَبُو عَبْدِ اللَّهِ: Abu Abdillah (a title for Imam Ja'far al-Sadiq or Imam al-Husayn)
key_terms.الْحَائِر: Al-Ha'ir (a specific location associated with Imam Husayn's journey or burial)
key_terms.شَارَكَ فِي دَمِهِ: Shared in his blood (participated in his killing)

ai.seo_question: What are the recommended prayers and phrases to recite when visiting the grave of Imam Husayn?
ai.summary: This narration from Ibn Qulawayh’s *Kamil al-Ziyarat* outlines the ritual protocol for visiting Imam al-Husayn’s grave and the specific site of his burial, al-Ha'ir, emphasizing the recitation of a concise yet potent supplication. It highlights the Shia practice of *al-lan* (invoking divine curse) upon the killers and their supporters, serving as a theological declaration of loyalty to the Ahl al-Bayt and disavowal of their enemies. This ritual reinforces the concept of *Bara'ah* (innocence from enemies) as an integral component of Ziyarah, connecting the physical act of visitation with spiritual allegiance.
